To find the required width, we need to factor the expression ${x}^{2}+3x-10.$

First, we find the factor pairs of the constant term $(-10).$ The constant term is negative, so that means one of the factors is negative, and the other is positive:

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & \times (-10) \\ (-1) & \times 10 \\ 2 & \times (-5) \\ (-2) & \times 5\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find which factor pair adds up to the coefficient of the linear term $3:$

$$
\begin{aligned}1+(-10) & =-9 & \times  \\ -1+10 & =9 & \times  \\ 2+(-5) & =-3 & \times  \\ -2+5 & =3 & ✓\end{aligned}
$$

Using the factor pair identified above, write the linear term as $3x=5x-2x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+3x-10 & ={x}^{2}+5x-2x-10\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we factor the first two terms and the last two terms separately, and then factor the expression completely:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+5x-2x-10 & = \\ ({x}^{2}+5x)+(-2x-10) & = \\ x(x+5)-2(x+5) & = \\ (x-2)(x+5)\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, we conclude that the width must be $x-2$ meters.
